comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Seen again 2026-09-26 at load average 36-50 during MIP-3 round 1: muster pane send's Return timed out twice (text landed, Return did not; pane read also timed out), and an empty --enter retried moments later worked. Integrator sends timed out repeatedly the same way. Under herdr the keystroke waits on its one render thread (a_2KHGXkKSc); MIP-3's daemon removes that thread, so re-check this after the cut-over rather than tuning the budget now.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-04: already true since the move off herdr - daemon requests wait a 10 s PATIENCE (muster-daemon-client backend.rs:32) and keystrokes ride a separate input connection. Closing.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Requests that come from the CLI still ride the 500ms budget `HerdrClient::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` gives keystrokes. A CLI request is not on the typing path, so nobody is waiting on it at keystroke speed, but it times out as though it were.

Since `5a5abb4` such a timeout reads as `unanswered` (exit 4) rather than as a refusal, which is honest. It still fails: the `daemon_settings` test flake is this. Whether CLI-originated intents should get the session's longer allowance instead is the decision this card is for.
title: CLI requests time out on the 500ms budget keystrokes get
